svg.title: Trellis brand sheet
svg.text: A fence lattice with a grown T — the two members that carry the T are bolder than the frame.
The trellis is drawn as a fence lattice: canes that thicken toward the base,
rails that bow, uneven member lengths — organic, not machined. The middle
post and top rail are the heaviest lines and read as a T; the T sits forward
and, in colour, is the only amber element.
Two colours, with a clear job each. The palette avoids the default blue of developer tools.

svg.text: Pine 5535 C (approx.) · Amber 143 C (approx.) — verify against a Pantone guide before print.
The T keeps its own colour on light and dark; in one-colour use it still reads because it is the heaviest element.
Every mark ships in full colour, one colour, and reversed.
Horizontal is primary. One unit = the width of a lattice cane.
Wordmark — where the symbol is already known
At 16 px the thin frame becomes texture — a simplified cut keeps the T sharp.

svg.text: Keep a margin of 1 × cane width (≈ 7 % of the mark) on all sides.
Nothing enters that zone — no type, no rules, no edges.
Symbol: 16 px screen / 6 mm print (use the small cut).
Horizontal lockup: 130 px wide screen / 34 mm print.
